about: The short state of the project. Read it first; DESIGN.md has the detail and the evidence. Update it when a milestone, a decision or a dead end lands.

milestones.what: a release the friend can use on his Windows PC, running in WSL2: a guided WSL setup, a one-line install, a Start-menu shortcut, a local UI, tested on his PC
milestones.plan: docs/work-orders/M4-00-plan.md: v0.1 is a guide to set up WSL, install.sh fetched from the pre-release and checked by hash (uv lanes cu132/cu126/cpu, allin1's own Python, Node, autochart with its models and its CUDA 13 provider, doctor.json, a .wslconfig with Windows' RAM minus 4 GB, a Start-menu shortcut), device checks with the CPU fallback shown, the local UI in WSL opened in the Windows browser (drop, options, progress with cancel, the static preview, zip and install into the Windows Songs folder), diagnostics, and CI end to end in ubuntu:26.04. Native Windows and the rest are M4-99; the native plan is commit 6e7ab41 and M4-00's appendix.
risks: peak RAM with CUDA inside 12 GB of WSL memory (a 16 GB PC): on the 5070 with 22 GB of WSL memory the tree peaked at 11.09 GiB RSS (during the sections), on the CPU at 10.1 GB, allin1's runner 7.8 GB; M4-08 measures it with memory=12GB, swap 8 GB absorbs short peaks, and under 11 GB of WSL memory allin1 is left out (librosa sections)

autochart's CUDA provider in WSL needs CUDA 13 libraries (the cu132 lane's wheels plus nvidia-curand): it loaded and ran the guitar on the 5070 in M4-00b's spike and in the GPU smoke test; a driver under 580 leaves the guitar on the CPU. VRAM: 8,987 MiB at the peak of 12 GB, and the friend's 4070 has 12 GB with Windows' desktop holding some (M4-08 records the free VRAM)

the Start-menu shortcut under Smart App Control: a .lnk written from WSL has no Mark of the Web and targets the signed wsl.exe, so it should run; untested until M4-08 (fallback: open Ubuntu, type songcharter)
the Windows browser reaches the server through WSL's localhost forwarding (default on); the server checks it from Windows with curl.exe and falls back to WSL's own address
decisions: route: WSL2, not native Windows (the owner, 2026-11-03): the friend's PC has Smart App Control on, which blocks unsigned DLLs and Python modules with no per-app exception; Linux programs in WSL2 are outside it, and onnxruntime-node's Linux build gives the guitar CUDA again
delivery: a GitHub pre-release on neb882/song-charting (the owner)
licence: MIT for songcharter's own code, LICENSE on main (the owner); NOTICE lists the third parties
uninstall: the guide offers wsl --unregister Ubuntu as the complete uninstall, with a warning to use it only if that Ubuntu holds nothing else (the owner, 2026-11-03)

lyrics (M4-10, DESIGN 2.15): `--lyrics FILE` / Options.lyrics; the friend pastes the text, songcharter never looks lyrics up or transcribes; the aligner is torchaudio's English 960 h large CTC bundle with a star before every line, chosen by measurement on the six references' 1,277 human-timed words (0.915 within 250 ms on the stems; the multilingual bundle 0.854, ctc-forced-aligner 0.812); the text goes into notes.chart only, every report counts it

memory rule: Windows' RAM rounded up to a whole GB, then less 4 (the owner, 2026-11-04, at the release gate: reported RAM is always a little under what is installed, so a PC sold as 16 GB that reports 15.4 GiB gets memory=12GB, not 11); allin1 is left out at 14 GiB or less, 11 GiB or less is refused

takes: 4 guitar takes stay the CUDA default after the GPU smoke test (4 takes cost 3.9 times one, not the 3.41 assumed: 854 s of a 959 s cold chart of a 412 s song), decided at the release gate with the owner's go-ahead, 2026-11-04

a guitar take that fails on CUDA: v0.1 says what to try (close programs that use the GPU and chart again, or Guitar takes 1, then Device CPU) and keeps the finished takes; no CPU retry until M4-08 has measured the friend's free VRAM (the advisor's finding 1, the skeptic's option (a); the rc-fixes brief, 2026-11-04)

Release gate: the lyrics aligner's first-use download (1.26 GB) shows no progress on the page (only the lyrics stage running); its lines every 50 MB go to the job's log. Since the review of the gate fixes it goes through runtime.download_part, so it is retried, and a cut one is resumed by the next song with lyrics. Release gate: an install made before songcharter's own uv cache (runtime/uv-cache) keeps its ~/.cache/uv, which songcharter no longer counts or deletes. Its next run downloads nothing into the new cache while its environments are complete: checked with uv 0.13.5 (the pinned tarball) on a setuptools project installed --no-editable, whose re-sync with an empty cache, offline too, only 'Checked 2 packages'. A new release (the app at a new path) rebuilds songcharter's wheel, which needs setuptools: one small download (4.4 MB of cache with the index pages), plus what the new lock changes; offline that rebuild fails. v0.1 is not released, so only dev and CI installs have an old cache.

[M5-08] Release gate: the install's closing summary prints doctor.json as step 8 wrote it, before WSL restarts with the memory step 9 set (on a 16 GB PC with no .wslconfig, 'WSL has 7.8 GB ... allin1 is left out'). The page's header and diagnostics' doctor-now.json measure it again; the GPU is not measured again in the header. The advisor on the release candidate (finding 7) and its skeptic: on a PC that reports under about 15.2 GiB the summary also shows the problem 'WSL has 7.4 GB of memory, under 8 GB' and 'doctor: 1 problem', and install.sh exits 1 after the restart it runs (nothing is skipped; the exit code is never seen). The fix, later: when step 9 wrote .wslconfig (its flag), drop the WSL-memory problem and the two memory notes from the summary, end with 'WSL's memory is measured again after the restart', and take the exit code from the problems left. It must not hide the disk and component problems, nor the memory problem when no restart follows (.wslconfig kept, a No, or a rerun after an interrupted restart, whose 'kept' sets no flag), and plain Linux and CI (no flag) stay as they are. M4-08 records the install's last lines.

GPU smoke test: song.ogg differs between two charts of the same song only in each Ogg page's serial number and checksum (notes.chart and song.ini identical), against the rule that the same input gives byte-identical output.
